summary:
When we picture space exploration, we imagine new rockets and fresh headlines. But out on the Moon, on Mars, and in the dark between the stars, robotic explorers that finished their missions are quietly holding decades of scientific history.

Monuments Among the Stars: A Young Explorer’s Guide to NASA’s Off-World Hardware is an illustrated digital field guide for ages 10–15 that gives these machines a voice. Answering the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, it tells the stories of four iconic NASA missions: Apollo 11’s Eagle descent stage and laser reflectors, the Opportunity rover, the InSight lander, and Voyager 1.

Each chapter combines vivid storytelling with quick mission facts, a “Why It Still Matters” science takeaway, and a fun fact. A timeline, glossary, and “Think Like a Scientist” questions invite readers to wonder, not just memorize.

By turning forgotten hardware into stories, we hope to spark young learners’ curiosity about planetary science and show that exploration leaves a legacy long after the engines go quiet.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Monuments Among the Stars: A Young Explorer’s Guide to NASA’s Off-World Hardware is an 8-page illustrated field guide for curious readers aged 10 to 15. It answers the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge by asking a simple question: what happens to a spacecraft after the headlines move on?

Each of the four chapters follows the same pattern, so readers always know where they are: a Mission File with the key facts, The Story, Why It Still Matters, and a Fun Fact.

  • Apollo 11 (the Moon): Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin’s landing craft left its lower half behind, and a mirror-like array of glass prisms still bounces laser beams back to Earth. Those beams show that the Moon is drifting away from us by about 3.8 cm every year.
  • Opportunity (Mars): This solar-powered rover was built for 90 Martian days. It kept going for almost 15 years and drove more than 45 km. Along the way it found “Martian blueberries,” tiny mineral spheres that helped prove water once soaked ancient Mars.
  • InSight (Mars): This lander never moved. It sat still, like a doctor with a stethoscope, and listened to more than 1,300 marsquakes. That revealed what Mars’s crust and liquid metal core are like.
  • Voyager 1 (deep space): This is humanity’s farthest traveller. In November 2026 it reaches one light-day from Earth, about 25.9 billion km. It is still tasting the particles between the stars and carrying the Golden Record with it.

The guide ends with an Explorer’s Toolkit: a timeline of the missions, a plain-language glossary, and “Think Like a Scientist” questions that invite readers to wonder, not just memorize.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Active missions grab the attention, and the machines that paved the way get forgotten. We wanted to change that. By turning geology, seismology and deep-space travel into stories a 12-year-old can follow, the guide connects space history with real STEM learning. It also nudges young readers to ask how scientists know what they know, and what instruments could help them find out more. We hope it leaves them curious about the missions still to come.

Creativity & Design Factors Considered

We didn’t want an encyclopedia entry. We wanted something that feels like a real explorer’s field guide: a deep-space navy palette with gold and cyan accents, original vector artwork, and short, vivid sections written for middle-grade readers. We kept the text high-contrast and easy to read, and we checked the facts against NASA’s official mission pages. We also made sure it follows NASA Space Apps branding rules. Every illustration is original, and there are no NASA logos or insignia anywhere.

Tools & Software Used

  • Research & fact-checking: NASA’s official mission archives (science.nasa.gov/moon/, mer-opportunity/, insight/ and voyager/).
  • Writing, layout & design: Our own text, with AI tools helping with editing, proofreading, fact-checking support and layout design. The typography, timeline graphics and vector artwork were built in code and exported as a PDF.
  • Hosting & presentation: Google Drive (public view-only PDF) and a 7-slide pitch deck.
